assessment: This work sets out to develop a better machine learning-based predictor of survival/prognosis for patients diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. To achieve this, the authors developed a large combinatorial family of machine learning methods based on a high-dimensional set of -omics and other patient data features; using ten publicly available data sets. By finding the combined ML method(s) that performed best on the task, the authors were able to identify a reduced set of features (giving rise to a signature called AIDPS that involves 9 genes) which, when measured in the patient, allow for fairly accurate prediction of patient survival and prognosis. Importantly, three new external data sets GSE21501, GSE57495, GSE71729 were used in the validation.
